claims_checked.claim: Some people in Japan bow during telephone calls even though the other party cannot see them.
claims_checked.note: Widely observed in service and office settings; not universal.

claims_checked.claim: The other party can sense the bow through the phone.
The movement is related to in-person ojigi and keigo, amplified by service training.
claims_checked.note: Presented as interpretation of embodied politeness + scripts.

claims_checked.claim: Younger people and casual calls do it less.
claims_checked.note: Register/role variation; not a census statistic.

claims_checked.claim: All Japanese people bow on every call.
claims_checked.note: Article lists exceptions: friends, trains, casual shops.

caveats_about_absolutes: Note regional, generational, and situational variation
